rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_source.fn` is one sentence: "Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read_source` for this operation." It is a usage convention for code that consumers write. It does not prescribe a library, algorithm, signature, type or field for any item in this crate. There are no review roots and no acknowledgments.

I considered the clause "uses ... read_source" as a delegation obligation. It binds criterion code, which is outside the SDK's own items. The SDK's part is to provide the method. The signature, resolution, reading and recording of that method belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read_source` and its refinements. Those declarations are assessed on their own text. The method is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'_, D>]/fn[read_source]`. It maps the item with `self.graph.source_node` and then reads through `self.read`.

A rewrite of the SDK method that kept the same behavior would still satisfy this sentence. The sentence only says that consumers call the method. A criterion that bypasses the method is a defect in that criterion's code. It does not make an SDK item missing an {impl}. Tests do exercise the use. For example, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/impl[ReadSource/Criterion<Project>]/fn[execute]` calls `cx.read_source`.

No structural obligation here needs implementation evidence. The cited requirement is the context, and nothing is missing.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_source.fn` says only that criterion code uses `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read_source` for this operation. That is a structural or usage choice. It has no independent observable behavior of its own. The behavior it points to is the cited requirement's: resolve an outline item, read it, and record the observation. That requirement has its own implementation and tests, and I did not reassess them.

The subject is also marked by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[direct_source_reads_preserve_mapping_errors_and_record_only_successful_returns]`. That test calls `ValidationContext::read_source` directly. It covers these cases:

- Unmappable addresses return an error, record no dependency and cause no read.
- A provider read failure is passed through and records no dependency.
- A successful read returns the content and records a `Dependency::Node` with its fingerprint.
- The record created from those dependencies is current, then stale after the content changes.

That is more than the subject needs. I found no unmet obligation and no marker gap.
